title: Lab CV
intro: Teach a model to recognise images and see what it looks at to decide. Everything runs on your device.

challenges.title: Challenges with prepared photos
challenges.intro: Each challenge brings a set of photos with a hidden trap. Load it, train the model in “Tools” and use the heat map to find out what it really looks at.
challenges.trapLabel: Hint (open it once you have tried)
challenges.missing: This challenge’s photos are not there yet. Whoever sets up the site must place them in {{folder}} (see public/datasets/README.md).
challenges.waitBackbone: Wait for the base model to finish loading.
challenges.failed: The challenge could not be loaded. Try again.

huskyWolf.title: Husky or wolf?
huskyWolf.story: A model has to tell huskies from wolves. It is almost always right… but does it look at the animal?
huskyWolf.task: Train the model and explain the test photos. Which part of the photo does the heat map colour?
huskyWolf.trap: In the training photos every wolf is on snow. The model can learn “snow = wolf” and call a husky in the snow a wolf. That is a shortcut: right for the wrong reason.

fewCats.title: Lots of dogs, few cats
fewCats.story: This set has loads of dog photos and very few cat photos.
fewCats.task: Train and look at the results per class. Is it as good with cats as with dogs?
fewCats.trap: With few examples of a class, the model tends to answer the majority class. Overall accuracy can look good while it gets cats wrong almost every time. Try balancing the classes and training again.

orangeBall.title: Orange or ball?
orangeBall.story: Oranges and balls: both are round. What does the model use to tell them apart?
orangeBall.task: Train the model and explain an orange ball. Compare the heat map with occlusion.
orangeBall.trap: If the training balls are colourful and the oranges are orange, the model may learn colour alone. An orange ball gives it away.

missions.title: Missions
missions.intro: A path through the Lab CV. Each mission has something to do and a question to think about. Your answers are kept on this device only.

teach.title: Teach it to see
teach.what: A model learns from the examples you give it, not from rules.
teach.challenge: Create a class for each thing you want to recognise (2 or more), capture at least 10 photos of each and train.
teach.question: What do you think the model has learned from your photos?

heatmap.title: Read the heat map
heatmap.what: The heat map colours the parts of the image that weighed most in the decision.
heatmap.challenge: Freeze an image and ask for the explanation.
heatmap.question: Does the model look where you expected? If not, where?

shortcut.title: Catch a shortcut
shortcut.what: Sometimes the model is right for the wrong reason, such as the photo’s background.
shortcut.challenge: Load the “Husky or wolf?” challenge, train and explain the test photos.
shortcut.question: Which shortcut did the model learn, and how did you find out?

imbalance.title: Balance the data
imbalance.what: If one class has many more photos than another, the model can be unfair to the small one.
imbalance.challenge: Load “Lots of dogs, few cats”, train, look at the results per class and train again with balanced classes.
imbalance.question: What changed when you balanced the classes? Who would this mistake harm in a real app?

twoExplanations.title: Two explanations
twoExplanations.what: The heat map and occlusion are two different ways of explaining the same decision.
twoExplanations.challenge: Compare both explanations of the same image.
twoExplanations.question: Do they agree? If not, which do you trust more and why?

fool.title: Fool the model
fool.what: Breaking a model on purpose is the best way to see its limits.
fool.challenge: Find an image the model gets wrong with high confidence and explain it.
fool.question: Why was it wrong? Which photos would you add to fix it?
